newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian blue chips further depress share trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian blue chips further depress share trade.

text.p: Nigerian blue chip stocks fell heavily on the stock market on Monday amid persistent selling, traders said.
The all-share index was unchanged from its 8415.74 close on Friday.
Traders said there were few buyers of the leading stocks as investors continued to dump them, believing they were overpriced.
"Price adjustment will continue until the market considers the shares attrractive again," one said.
Prices have been falling in the face of dwindling returns from the firms, blamed on Nigeria's economic woes.
Monday's biggest loser was Lever Brothers, down 60 kobo at 26.50 naira.
African Petroleum closed at 54.50 naira, 40 kobo lower, the same as PZ Industries which finished at 26.30 naira.

Nigerian Bottling Company fell 25 kobo to 52.60 naira, Nigerian Breweries shed 10 kobo at 18.15 naira and Union Bank slid to 9.00 naira, down 35 kobo, all of them on the continuing dumping of blue chip stocks.
The market was cool to Ashaka Cement's half-year result showing after-tax profits to 280 million naira in the period to end-May against 247.4 million naira a year earlier.
But improved perception favoured United Bank for Africa (UBA), which rose five kobo to 12.75 naira.
Dealers said speculation gave West African Portland Cement Company a hefty 35 kobo rise to close at 61.00 naira.
Construction firm Cappa and D'Alberto also fared well, ending 10 kobo higher at 12.50 naira.
Textile group Afprint gained four kobo to 2.40 naira on its recent improved full year result.
